# EnterpriseGlue v0.20.3 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.20.2`.

## Highlights

- **plugins:** Makes OSS the sole EnterpriseGlue product host and routes independently delivered capabilities through public plugin contracts.
- **packages:** Publishes externally consumable shared and host packages without unresolved pnpm workspace protocol dependencies.
- **continuous-integration:** Authenticates private host-package downloads during reusable source-image validation.

## User and administrator impact

- The EnterpriseGlue OSS application remains the product host; independently delivered plugins continue to install through the supported plugin platform.
- External plugin consumers can refresh lockfiles after an OSS release without pnpm treating @enterpriseglue/plugin-sdk as a missing local workspace package.
- Enterprise consumers can run the shared source-image CI gate without an unauthorized package download failure.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- No host upgrade action is required; plugin owners should qualify against the supported OSS host and plugin API versions.
- Package consumers should update @enterpriseglue/shared to 0.15.2, @enterpriseglue/backend-host to 0.13.3, and @enterpriseglue/frontend-host to 0.15.2 together.

## Database migrations

- No database schema or persisted data changes are included.
- This CI-only fix does not change application schemas, migrations, TypeORM behavior, or supported database adapters.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Removes obsolete OSS automation credentials and repository dispatches that targeted the retired standalone EE delivery path.
- The package payload is unchanged except for resolving internal workspace dependency declarations to immutable published versions.
- The reusable workflow passes its existing least-privilege package token only to the Docker dependency-install build argument.

## Documentation

- Updates contributor architecture, release guidance, and Codex workflows for the OSS-host and independent-plugin model.
- The generated release notes describe the corrected public package dependency contract and coordinated package versions.
- The generated technical release notes describe the repaired reusable CI authentication contract.

## Rollback

- Revert the workflow and documentation commit; no data rollback is required.
- Consumers can restore their previous lockfile and package versions; no database or configuration rollback is required.
- Revert the workflow change to restore the previous behavior; no application or database rollback is required.

## Validation evidence

- CI contract tests reject future OSS workflow dispatches to the retired EE repository.
- The versioned Codex plugin and every bundled skill pass the repository and official validators.
- CI packs every public package and rejects workspace protocol dependencies in the external manifest.
- A clean external-consumer install validates the packed shared and host package set.
- The workspace runtime contract requires the reusable source-image build to pass its package token.
- CI contract tests and workflow lint validate the reusable workflow.
